summary.summary: Thanet's borrowing is scaling up fast to fund a £189.6m revised 2026/27 capital programme: gross debt stood at £90.5m at 30 June 2026, up from £37.1m a year earlier, and the council's underlying need to borrow (the Capital Financing Requirement) is forecast to nearly double from £92.2m at March 2026 to £180.4m by March 2027 — close under the £191m authorised borrowing limit. A £10m ten-year PWLB loan was drawn in May 2026 at the 4.95% HRA concessionary rate for council-housing capital works. Investments were £44.4m (of which £40.2m in money market funds, all maturities under one year) yielding 3.90% against a 3.75% SONIA benchmark, and the s151 officer reports no limit breaches in the quarter and no difficulties envisaged in complying with the prudential indicators.
summary.as_of_doc: Quarter 1 Review 2026/27: Treasury Management and Annual Investment Strategy

signals.headline: Gross debt £90.5m at 30 June 2026 vs £37.1m at 30 June 2025; CFR forecast to rise from £92.2m (March 2026) to £180.4m (March 2027), against a £191m authorised limit — includes a £10m 10-year PWLB EIP loan drawn 29 May 2026 at 4.95%
signals.why: Debt has more than doubled in a year and is planned to roughly double again within twelve months to finance a £189.6m capital programme, a very large build-out for a small district that narrows headroom under the statutory limit.

news_drafts.headline: Thanet's reserves fall below safety floor as two years of service overspends erode financial cushion
news_drafts.lead: Thanet has drawn reserves down to £4.1m of unrestricted funds, falling below the £6m floor its chief finance officer has advised the authority maintain as it heads toward Local Government Reorganisation. The decline reflects two consecutive years of overspend: £4.7m in 2024-25 and £3.5m in 2025-26, driven by structural deficits in three major service areas totalling £2.26m. Temporary Accommodation overspent by £597k on nightly-paid costs, Housing Benefit incurred a £662k shortfall because central government froze subsidy rates at January 2011 levels, and Domestic Waste and Street Cleansing overspent £1.001m on agency cover and emergency vehicle hire. The council's capital programme delivered only £28.6m of its £80.6m budget; the shortfall reflects a £21.9m miss on external funding expected from grants. The 2026-27 forecast indicates service pressures are highly likely to exceed £1m further, and the council faces unfunded transition costs of £700k to £1.2m as it prepares for reorganisation.

news_drafts.headline: Thanet council overspends £8.2m in two years, reserves fall below advised floor
news_drafts.lead: Thanet council overspent by £4.7m in 2024-25 and £3.5m in 2025-26, leaving reserves of just £5.1m with only £4.1m available to spend on unexpected costs. This falls below the £6m floor advised by its chief finance officer, particularly as local government reorganisation approaches. Despite introducing weekly spending controls on orders over £10,000 from mid-2025-26, the final overspend grew from a £2.9m forecast to £3.5m. Three service areas recorded recurring pressures: temporary accommodation (£597k overspend on emergency nightly housing), housing benefit subsidy (£662k shortfall from rates frozen since 2011), and waste services (£1m overspend on agency cover). A preliminary 2026-27 forecast indicates service pressures "highly likely" to exceed £1m overspend, while local government reorganisation transition costs of £700,000 to £1.2m remain unfunded.

news_drafts.headline: Thanet reserves fall below safety level as overspends persist despite spending controls
news_drafts.lead: Thanet Council's reserves have fallen to £4.1m of unrestricted money, below the £6m floor its chief finance officer has advised it maintain. The shortfall follows a second consecutive year of major overspending: £4.7m in 2024-25 and £3.5m in 2025-26. Despite introducing weekly spending panels and vacancy freezes, the council's day-to-day running costs exceeded budget across three major service areas. Temporary accommodation overspent by £597k, waste and cleansing by £1.001m, and housing benefit subsidy fell £662k short—all described as ongoing structural deficits rather than one-off problems. An early forecast for 2026-27 indicates a further overspend exceeding £1m is highly likely, offset only by a non-recurring collection fund surplus. The council is preparing for local government reorganisation with transition costs estimated at £700k to £1.2m and no identified funding source.

findings.headline: All figures in report are provisional pending publication of final Statements of Account
findings.detail: The treasury management report presents year-end figures as provisional, noting that final Statements of Account for 2025/26 have not yet been published. The council indicates that members will be updated of any material changes that arise from the final accounts process.
findings.matters: Audited accounts are authoritative; reported figures may change materially during the accounts process, affecting materiality of treasury position
findings.quote: The Council has not yet published its final Statements of Account for 2025/26 so the figures in this report are subject to change. Members will be updated, at future meetings, of any material changes that arise.

findings.headline: Housing Revenue Account borrowing now exceeds its financing requirement by £3.7m for the first time
findings.detail: The HRA is now in an overborrowed position, with gross debt of £55.0m exceeding the Capital Financing Requirement of £51.3m. While the overall council shows underborrowing of £11.2m (General Fund underborrowed by £15.0m offset by HRA overborrowing of £3.7m), the council's treasury strategy indicates this HRA overborrowing will be resolved within the next two financial years.
findings.matters: Overborrowing exceeds prudential borrowing limits and indicates timing mismatch between debt taken and capital spending; though mitigated by expected resolution
findings.figures: HRA debt £55.009m vs CFR £51.266m; HRA overborrowing £3.7m; overall underborrowing £11.247m (GF underborrowing £15.0m, HRA overborrowing £3.7m)
findings.quote: The overall CFR underfunding of £11.3m is comprised of £15.0m GF underfunding and £(3.7)m HRA overfunding. As per section 6.5.1 above, it is estimated that this HRA overfunding will be utilised within the next two financial years.

findings.headline: Council shifted from net investment position of £1.7m to net debt of £48.3m
findings.detail: At 31 March 2025, the council had investments of £35.4m exceeding debt of £37.1m, creating a net investment position of £1.7m. By 31 March 2026, with debt increased to £80.9m and investments decreased to £32.7m, the council was in a net debt position of £48.3m. This represents a swing of approximately £50m in the council's net cash position.
findings.matters: Net debt position reflects the council's overall cash strength and financial flexibility; deterioration indicates reduced headroom and increased reliance on borrowing
findings.figures: Net position shifted from £1.746m net investment (March 2025) to £48.254m net debt (March 2026); gross debt £80.926m, investments £32.672m
findings.quote: This table also shows that the Council's investments totalled £32.672m at the 2025/26 year end and therefore was in a net debt position, as debt held exceeded investments by £48.254m.

findings.headline: Interest rates on new council borrowing increased from 4.16% to 4.97% between July 2025 and March 2026
findings.detail: The council took five PWLB loans during 2025/26, with rates rising from 4.16% in July to 4.97% in March. Gilt yields rose substantially through the year, with particularly steep increases in March 2026 due to inflation concerns related to the Middle East conflict. This resulted in higher borrowing costs than might have been expected earlier in the financial year.
findings.matters: Rising cost of capital increases council service costs and reduces affordability of future borrowing; indicates a challenging market environment
findings.quote: Gilt yields have been volatile through 2025/26. The low point for long-term rates of 25 and 50 years duration was reached early in April 2025 whilst the low points for short and medium dated rates were reached in early 2026, prior to the outbreak of the Middle East conflict.

findings.headline: Capital expenditure was £59.0m against a budget of £159.6m, delivering only 37% of planned investment
findings.detail: The council budgeted £159.6m of capital expenditure for 2025/26 but delivered only £59.0m, representing a 63% underspend. This comprised General Fund £29.8m against budget £79.6m and HRA £29.2m against budget £80.0m. The council has acknowledged significant slippage in the capital programme as an issue requiring action.
findings.matters: Major capital programme underspend suggests project management or delivery constraints; indicates capital assets and improvements are being delayed
findings.figures: £159.6m budgeted, £59.0m actual; General Fund £79.6m budget vs £29.8m actual; HRA £80.0m budget vs £29.2m actual
findings.quote: Slippage will not be an acceptable norm. Capital schemes will be at risk of having their Council funding re-directed should there be delays that cannot be substantiated (schemes that are externally funded may require more flexibility however).
